new_findings_today.title: qa/_lib/build_report.js buildBusiness() traffic-light table rendered empty status/why cells in every prior week's Business Report
new_findings_today.detail: bs.traffic_lights.map(t => [t.area, t.status, t.why]) expected {area,status,why} object shape, but SKILL.md documents (and every findings.json, including the 09-03 worked example, actually stores) traffic_lights as [area, status, why] ARRAYS. Since arrays have no .area/.status/.why properties, every row rendered three empty cells under correct 'Area/Status/Why' headers -- verified by generating a business report from findings/2026-09-03.json and confirming the same empty-cell pattern, so this has silently affected every historical run, not just today's. Caught only because SKILL.md's own verification discipline (scan the generated .docx text, don't just re-read the generator code) was followed literally this run. Fixed with a one-line defensive change (_lib/build_report.js:196) that accepts both array and object shapes; verified the regenerated table now shows real green/yellow statuses and explanatory text for all 11 rows.
new_findings_today.evidence: unzip -p NakshIQ_Business_Report.docx word/document.xml | grep Traffic-light -A1 (before/after fix)
new_findings_today.recommendation: Consider a small snapshot/golden-file test on qa/_lib/build_report.js's table-building functions so a data-shape mismatch like this fails CI instead of silently shipping an empty table for months.

business_summary.headline: The site is healthy and fast. All 10 sampled destination pages, the homepage, and every core section loaded correctly in both English and Hindi, with no broken pages, no server errors, and no missing photos anywhere in the 533-destination catalog. This week's automated check also caught something genuinely useful: today's random 10-destination sample happened to include 3 of the site's older-template destinations alongside the 7 newer-template ones, which finally let us confirm -- with real evidence instead of a guess -- exactly which pages have the Hindi-headline display issue and which don't. That distinction had been suspected for weeks but unconfirmed because recent weekly samples kept landing entirely on the newer template.
traffic_lights: Every page we checked loaded correctly -- 10/10 destinations, all core sections, both languages.
All 533 destinations have verified emergency numbers on file; the 10 we sampled averaged 7-8 working phone numbers each.
All 12 pages we checked have correct titles, canonical links, and social-preview images -- nothing for search engines to trip on.

Hindi pages load correctly and have correct Hindi titles everywhere. On a specific subset of destination pages (the ones using the newer 'cinematic' page design), the big headline still shows in English instead of Hindi -- known issue, being tracked.
A handful of destination web addresses

About 10 destinations happen to share a name with an Indian state (like Goa or Sikkim). A few unusual web addresses built from those names don't show the expected 'not found' page. Low real-world impact -- ordinary visitors won't hit this.
Two internal automations (a newsletter-delivery check and a destination-data refresher) have open questions from prior weeks that weren't re-investigated this run to keep the check efficient.
This check is meant to run daily but is actually only running once a week (every Monday) -- a configuration issue with the schedule itself, not the website. Flagged for Ashish to fix.
Looked at the last 7 days of server error logs: only 2 small, self-recovered hiccups, both affecting a single visitor each, with no visitor-facing failures. Nothing resembling an outage or a spike.
Subscriber count, send count, and open/click events all grew steadily week-over-week, with no signs of the list stalling or churning.

The itinerary-builder and weather-lookup services that power the site's planning tools were tested with both valid and deliberately broken requests. Valid requests returned real, complete trip plans; broken requests were rejected cleanly with a helpful error instead of crashing -- exactly the behavior you want from a production API.

The site's 'install as an app' and offline-fallback features (used by visitors who add NakshIQ to their phone's home screen) are all working: the install manifest, the background service worker, and the offline page all loaded correctly.

All 5 chunks of the site's master URL list loaded correctly, listing just over 25,000 pages for search engines to discover -- up slightly from last week, consistent with normal ongoing content growth.
Checked live in a real browser: the destination-explorer map (with all 519 destination markers) and both individual destination-page map styles all rendered correctly with no errors.
whats_changed: A new version of the site was deployed sometime this past week, along with a small database update -- both look routine, no problems found.

This week's random sample of 10 destinations happened to include 3 that use the site's older, simpler page template -- which let us directly confirm the Hindi-headline issue only affects the newer 'cinematic' template, not the older one.

One isolated, self-recovered slow-database moment was logged for a single destination page (mahabaleshwar) earlier in the week -- the page still loaded correctly for the visitor, just via a fallback path. Worth a quick look if it happens again.

Search-engine metadata (page titles, canonical links, language-alternate tags, and social preview images) was checked across 12 different page types this week and came back perfect on every single one -- no regressions from last week's equally clean result.

The emergency-contact-information system was re-verified for the full catalog of 533 destinations directly against the database (not just the 10 spot-checked pages) -- every single destination still has a complete, verified set of emergency numbers on file, unchanged from last week.

The internal report-writing tool used to produce this document was found to have a small display bug (an empty status table) and was fixed this run -- full detail is in the 'About this report' section at the end.
risks: The Hindi-headline issue (yellow above) affects an estimated majority of destinations, since the newer template is now the more common one. It does not break the page -- Hindi visitors still get a fully translated page, just with an English headline at the top.
The weekly (instead of daily) schedule for this QA check means a problem that appears and gets fixed within the same week could be missed entirely.
None of the open items this week are urgent or visitor-facing -- everything flagged above is either cosmetic, an edge case, or an internal process question.

The 10-destination sample is a snapshot, not a full audit -- while all 533 destinations were checked in bulk for emergency contacts and photos, the deeper per-page checks (search-engine metadata, live map rendering, Hindi headline behavior) only directly touched 10-12 pages this week. The sample is re-randomized weekly, so different pages get their turn over time.

The single self-recovered slow-database event and the 2 small server-error groups mentioned above are each isolated, single-visitor occurrences from earlier in the week rather than anything currently ongoing -- included here for completeness and trend-tracking, not because either represents a live problem right now.

As the newer 'cinematic' page template becomes more common across the catalog over time, the number of destinations affected by the Hindi-headline display gap will grow proportionally unless the underlying template issue is addressed directly, rather than shrinking on its own.
bottom_line: Nothing is broken for visitors today. The one thing worth Ashish's attention is the QA check's own schedule -- it should be running daily as intended but is actually configured to run weekly.
